Amino acids in proteins are connected through covalent bonds formed between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another, releasing a water molecule. This specific type of covalent bond is known as a peptide bond.  
Hydrogen bonds and ionic bonds are non-covalent interactions, not the primary linkages in the protein backbone. Glycosidic bonds connect sugar monomers in carbohydrates, not amino acids in proteins.
